packageRules.description: Auto-merge devDependency patch and minor bumps. Every one of these is gated on the CI workflow: Renovate will not merge a PR whose checks have not passed.
Patch bumps of runtime dependencies ship to consumers, so only the patch range auto-merges.
Majors always get a human. CI passing proves this package still builds, not that the upgrade is right for the people installing it.
peerDependencies are the public contract - changing a range changes what consumers are allowed to install. Widen rather than pin, and never merge unattended.
TypeScript and @types/node set the type-checking floor. A minor of either can introduce errors that CI catches but that need a judgement call rather than a merge.
Nest packages move together and are the framework this instruments; upgrading one without the others is rarely what you want.
Group the remaining tool families so a routine week is a few PRs rather than a dozen.
GitHub Actions are pinned by tag; digest bumps are noise worth merging automatically.
